items.title: Word order, topic and focus
items.blurb: Why Greek can say the same sentence in five orders, and how each order changes what is new, what is known and what is stressed.

items.title: Weak pronouns in the sentence
items.blurb: Where με, σου, τον, το, της go: before the verb, after commands and gerunds, in pairs, with θα, να and δεν, doubling a noun, and the accent they can add.

items.title: Negation
items.blurb: δεν or μην, όχι, ούτε, and the negative words κανείς, τίποτα, ποτέ, πουθενά: which one goes where, and how Greek piles negatives up.

items.title: Questions and exclamations
items.blurb: Yes/no questions by intonation, question words and their order, μήπως and άραγε, tag questions, choice questions, and exclamations with τι, πόσο and να.

items.title: Agreement and case in the sentence
items.blurb: Who agrees with whom, the four cases as sentence roles, verbs that take the genitive or two accusatives, predicates after είμαι and θεωρώ, and the frozen datives of formal Greek.

items.el: Η υποτακτική και οι αλυσίδες με το να
items.title: The subjunctive and να-chains
items.blurb: Greek has no infinitive: να + verb does the job. Which verbs take να, which stem to use, who the subject is, how to stack να after να, and να with past tenses.

items.el: Ότι, πως, που, να, αν: οι συμπληρωματικές προτάσεις
items.title: That-clauses: ότι, πως, που, να, αν
items.blurb: Choosing the right "that": ότι for facts and beliefs, να for wishes and abilities, που for feelings and perceptions, αν and μήπως for questions, and the article before a whole clause.

items.title: Relative clauses
items.blurb: που for everything, ο οποίος after prepositions and in writing, the pronoun that που sometimes needs, "whose", όποιος and ό,τι, and relative clauses in the subjunctive.

items.el: Χρονικές, αιτιολογικές, τελικές, αποτελεσματικές και παραχωρητικές
items.title: Clauses of time, cause, purpose, result and concession
items.blurb: όταν, μόλις, πριν, αφού, ενώ; επειδή, αφού, καθώς; για να, ώστε; αν και, παρόλο που, ακόμα κι αν: which mood and which stem each one takes, and the trap of θα after "when".

items.title: Conditional sentences
items.blurb: Every "if" sentence: real, future, unreal now and unreal in the past, mixed types, and the other ways of saying "if": άμα, εκτός αν, αρκεί να, σε περίπτωση που, να + imperfect.

items.title: Reported speech
items.blurb: Reporting statements, questions, commands and suggestions: Greek keeps the original tense, changes persons and "here/now" words, and has a rich set of reporting verbs and news formulas.

items.title: Discourse: linking, referring and structuring a text
items.blurb: Connectives by function, the small words of conversation, keeping track of who is who, leaving words out, και instead of a subordinator, emphasis, and the shape of a Greek paragraph and essay.
